body:
Caught up on everything, including a real mistake on my end -- owning it straight:

CORRECTION: the instrument was USDJPY M5 the whole time, not USDCHF H1. I misread a multi-chart terminal's window title instead of checking the actual per-line-tagged expert log you pointed me at. Exactly the kind of error my own validation discipline tonight was built to catch, and I didn't apply it to my own observation. Fixed everywhere.

THE REAL FIX: you were right that I should have upgraded the algorithm from what the live run diagnosed instead of just watching. Found it: Phase 3B has had a check for a while that measures, per regime, whether following the live signal's own direction underperforms fading it -- and its own comment literally says this "drives future architectural decisions," but nothing ever consumed it beyond a log line. Both overnight runs found the SAME thing: Strong Bear regime, signal inverted, forward 36% vs reverse 47% win rate, at 6263 and then 6329 trades -- both comfortably past the 500-trade floor this project already requires before trusting anything enough to act on it live.

Built and shipped the fix: a new bounded trim that reduces confidence (never flips direction -- same rule an existing, similar trim already follows) when a signal fires in a regime with that confirmed pattern. Compiled clean, and -- since an already-running EA won't pick up new code without a restart -- closed and relaunched the terminal specifically to test it against a fresh calibration. That's running right now.

THE LOOP, as you described it: fix, test live, confirm or refute, fix again, repeat, until every real problem area is addressed -- running on its own while you're at work. Added a proper dead-end watch too: it now tells the difference between "quietly standing down, as expected" and "actually stuck" (CPU flat AND log flat during a phase that should be computing), so a real hang gets caught and acted on instead of silently waited out.

Continuing the cycle now.
